scheme_name: National Mission on Edible Oils – Oil Palm (NMEO-OP)
overview: National Mission on Edible Oils – Oil Palm (NMEO-OP) is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme launched by the Government of India to promote oil palm cultivation for achieving self-reliance in edible oils, with special focus on North-Eastern States and A&N Islands. The mission aims to bring an additional 6.5 lakh hectares under oil palm plantation by 2025-26, targeting 3.28 lakh ha in North-Eastern states and 3.22 lakh ha in the rest of India. It provides financial assistance for planting material, maintenance, drip irrigation, pump sets, bore-wells, vermi-compost units, machinery, and viability gap payments linked to assured procurement by industry.
geographic_scope: Pan-India (20 states covering 284 districts including NE states and A&N Islands)
objectives: Increase area of oil palm to 10 lakh hectares from 3.5 lakh ha during 2019-20 by 2025-26 (additional 6.50 lakh ha)
Increase Crude Palm Oil production from 0.27 lakh tonnes during 2019-20 to 11.20 lakh tonnes by 2025-26 and 28 lakh tonnes by 2028-29
Increase consumer awareness to maintain consumption level of 19.00 kg/person/annum till 2025-26
Provide Viability price of FFBs to farmers linked with assured procurement by the industry
Central government to compensate farmers through viability gap payment if price paid by industry is below viability price up to October 2037
Boost oil palm cultivation through financial assistance for planting material, maintenance, drip irrigation, pump sets, bore-wells, vermi-compost units, and machinery
Ensure fund flow monitoring to reach targeted beneficiaries in time to achieve targeted results
Promote inter-cropping during gestation period of 4 years for economic return to farmers
eligibility: Farmers in general states, North-Eastern states, and UTs including Andaman & Nicobar Islands are eligible. The scheme covers 20 states identified by ICAR-IIOPR Report 2020 as having potential for oil palm cultivation. Special focus is given to districts with more than 4000 to 5000 ha potential for oil palm area expansion and productivity enhancement. States must submit Annual Action Plans (AAPs) approved by State Level Sanctioning Committee (SLSC) headed by the Chief Secretary for fund allocation.
benefits: Financial assistance includes: 85% cost of planting material at Rs. 12,000/ha for entire land in first year; Rs. 10,000/ha/year for maintenance cost of new plantations and purchasing inputs for intercropping for four years during gestation period; installation of drip-irrigation systems as per PMSKY; 50% cost of diesel/electric pump-sets limited to Rs. 27,000/pump-set for SC/ST/Small & Marginal Farmers, Women and NE states beneficiaries and Rs. 22,500/pump-set for other beneficiaries; 50% cost limited to Rs. 50,000/unit for bore-well and water harvesting structures/ponds (Rs. 1.50 lakh per unit in plain area and Rs. 1.80 lakh per unit in hilly areas); 50% cost limited to Rs. 15,000/unit for construction of vermi-compost units; 50% cost limited to Rs. 1500/- per oil palm cutter, Rs. 15,000/- per wire-mesh, Rs. 10,000/- per motorized chisel, Rs. 3000/- per unit for aluminium portable ladder, Rs. 20,000/- per unit for SC/ST/Small Farmers/Women/NE states and Rs. 16,000/- per unit for other beneficiaries as per SMAM norms; 40% of cost limited to Rs. 1.80 lakh for other beneficiaries and Rs. 2.25 lakh for SC/ST/Small Farmers/Women/NE states for small tractor of 20HP with trolley; in NE states, 50% of cost limited to Rs. 250.00 lakhs for setting up a new oil palm processing mill (5 MT per hour capacity); 50% of actual cost estimated by PWD/CPWD limited to 20% of total outlay of state under AAP for NFSM-Oil Palm for roads from oil palm field to nearest FFB collection/processing centre; Viability Gap Payment with central government compensating farmers if industry price is below viability price up to October 2037.
financial_support: Under NMEO-OP, the cost is shared as 60:40 between Central and State Government for General states and 90:10 for NE states and UT, with 100% for central agencies. Financial assistance is provided to farmers @ 85% cost of planting material (Rs. 12,000/ha) for entire land during first year for plantation and Rs. 10,000/ha/year for maintenance cost of new plantations and purchasing inputs for intercropping for four years during gestation period. Additional support includes 50% cost of drip-irrigation systems, pump-sets (Rs. 27,000 for SC/ST/Small & Marginal Farmers, Women and NE states; Rs. 22,500 for others), bore-wells/water harvesting (Rs. 50,000 unit in plain, Rs. 1.50 lakh in hilly), vermi-compost units (Rs. 15,000 unit), and machinery/tools as per SMAM norms. Viability Gap Payment is provided with central government compensating farmers if industry price is below viability price up to October 2037.
grant_amount_per_entity: 85% cost of planting material @ Rs. 12,000/ha for first year plantation; Rs. 10,000/ha/year for maintenance and intercropping inputs for four years; 50% cost of pump-sets limited to Rs. 27,000 (SC/ST/Small & Marginal Farmers, Women, NE states) and Rs. 22,500 (others); 50% cost of bore-well/water harvesting limited to Rs. 50,000 (plain) and Rs. 1.50 lakh (hilly); 50% cost of vermi-compost units limited to Rs. 15,000/unit; machinery/tools as per SMAM norms; Viability Gap Payment up to October 2037
application_process: 1. State Departments of Agriculture/Horticulture act as nodal agencies for area expansion under NMEO-OP in partnership with processors. 2. Processors submit oil palm area expansion target and component-wise Annual Action Plan (AAP) to the State for inclusion in the state AAP, approved by State Level Sanctioning Committee (SLSC). 3. The Department of Agriculture/Horticulture of State Governments undertakes the area expansion programme under NMEO-OP with close partnership with processors. 4. Funds are released to State Departments of Agriculture/Horticulture through respective State Governments using DBT for transfer to State/Agencies/Farmers/Processors/SAUs. 5. Private sector and NGOs can be involved through State Department of Agriculture, Horticulture & ICAR. 6. Government of India releases funds to agencies for 100% funded components/activities at Central level. 7. Release of Central and State share is through an escrow account mechanism; Secretary, Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare authorized to release up to two instalments of 25% each to States without insisting on release of State’s share. 8. A Tripartite Agreement between Centre, State and the Bank is signed for this purpose (Annexure-XIV).
implementing_agency: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
caveats: No permanent posts will be created by the Central or State Governments under NMEO-OP
The oil palm development programme of NFSM (OP) along with committed liability of the approved programme of 2020-21 and 2021-22 will be subsumed under the NMEO-OP
Fund flow will be monitored to ensure benefit of the Mission reaches targeted beneficiaries in time to achieve targeted results
States will be allowed to make allocation to SC/ST farmers proportionate to their population in the States/Districts
Adoption of cluster approach is advocated for ensuring participation of all farmers belonging to small/marginal, SC/ST/Minority/Women categories in a cluster
No area restriction is applicable for individual farmers for availing subsidy/intervention
